title: Covered call path dependency: AAPL weekly calls in 2025
summary: The speaker simulated selling at-the-money covered calls on Apple every week of 2025 for about 1% a week, or 52% a year. Apple fell in 25 of 52 weeks for a total of -86% on those weeks, while the upside was capped. Net, the program lost 34% in a year when the stock rose 9%. The path, not only the end price, decides the result.

steps.caption: One week of a weekly covered call on Apple, sold at the money.
The strike equals the price at entry. Any gain above it goes to the call buyer.
The price path: here a down week, about -4%. In 2025 Apple fell in 25 of 52 weeks.
Each week: collect about 1%. Over 52 weeks that is about 52% of premium.
Down weeks are not capped. The down weeks added up to -86%, so the net was about -34%.
Apple still ended 2025 up 9%. The order of the moves, the path, decided the result.

takeaways: A covered call caps the upside each week but keeps the full downside.
Weekly ATM calls on Apple in 2025: about +52% premium, -86% from down weeks, net about -34%.
The stock rose 9% that year, so the path, not the end price, drove the loss.
Collected premium is not the same as profit.
caveats: The simulation is the speaker's own; the method and resets are not shown, so the numbers are unverified.
The clip's transcript repeats words; the core numbers are 52%, 25 of 52 weeks, -86%, -34% and +9%.

backtest.note: Weekly at-the-money covered call on Apple through 2025, held to expiry, to test path dependency.
